correctness.rationale: Every nonnegative-determinant two-state transition is a nondecreasing affine map of the accepted-state probability. Dynamic programming gives the scalar monotone envelope G and its monotone orbit; uniqueness forces a unique active letter at each step. A signed affine difference cannot alternate positive-negative-positive along monotone points, prohibiting any repeated run. The explicit rational construction uses ordered line crossings, uniform perturbation <2r epsilon, and orbit error <4r epsilon, strictly smaller than the minimum crossing clearance. Thus the prescribed run-distinct word is uniquely optimal. Stochasticity and positive slopes follow from the explicit parameter inequalities. Exact rational checker replayed across 374 witness configurations and additional positive-slope necessity sanity checks. Enumeration follows bijectively from ordered distinct letters and positive compositions. The construction also proves that each rational transition entry has denominator dividing r times 2 to the power 2n+5, giving linear-in-length bit size.

originality.rationale: Gill (arXiv:2402.13376) classifies unrestricted binary two-state witnesses; its Section 4.4 transfers binary witnesses to larger alphabets but does not classify arbitrary-alphabet positive-determinant witnesses. Kjos-Hanssen (arXiv:2607.26275v1) proves the three-state upper bound and explicitly leaves the general ternary-or-larger two-state classification unresolved (Remark 5.3). The present theorem gives a new if-and-only-if characterization, rational construction, and enumerative formula for the order-preserving subclass on all alphabet sizes; the binary restriction follows from known broader binary work and is not independently claimed new. Several targeted current-literature and semantic-record queries did not reveal equivalent or dominating statements. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly identifies arbitrary-alphabet two-state complexity classification as a remaining gap. The natural order-preserving subclass has a complete if-and-only-if word-language characterization, an explicit rational stochastic witness for any prescribed admissible word, and an exact all-alphabet enumerative formula and generating function. This distinguishes positive-determinant transition dynamics from unrestricted binary alternating phenomena and provides a structural baseline for the open general multi-letter problem; it is not merely a renamed binary case or an unmotivated finite table. Transition probabilities require only O(n+log r) bits per entry, so the classification has an effective, explicit resource bound.
